#4492 release matrix -- predicate clauses, shader shapes, raw offsets

Generated by measure.py (committed beside this file); every command below
is echoed exactly as executed, via subprocess.list2cmdline.

args (identical for every shader and every release): -T cs_6_2 -E testStructuredBufferMatrixLoad2 -enable-16bit-types

  repro    repro.hlsl                        match.json        the reporter's attached shader, verbatim; correct span <= 32
  minimal  minimal-matrix.hlsl               match.json        the issue body's own snippet, a[0].xy + a[3].zw; correct 0,2,28,30
  ld-ctrl  control-half-vec-array.hlsl       match.json        NEGATIVE CONTROL for match.json: half4 v[4]; correct 0,2,...,30
  store    store-matrix.hlsl                 match-store.json  store direction, a[0][1] and a[3][3]; correct 2 and 30
  st-ctrl  control-store-half-vec-array.hlsl match-store.json  NEGATIVE CONTROL for match-store.json: half4 v[4]; correct 2 and 30

Every shader declares a 32-byte $Element. Correct codegen keeps every
rawBufferLoad/Store.f16 inside [0,32). 'span' is the highest byte touched,
computed as offset + 2 * popcount(mask), so 'past the end' is a number.

Both predicates are an AND of three clauses:
  A = anchor/self-test: the f16 buffer op the predicate reads is present
  E = element-size self-test: $Element reported as 32 bytes
  S = symptom: some such op has elementOffset >= 32
A and E are the instrument. If either flips while S does not, that
release is unmeasurable under that predicate, NOT clean. Both clause sets
are shown for every row; 'scored' marks the one that shader is judged by.

prereleases excluded from the sequence by policy: v1.5.2003

Read the summary this way:
  ld-ctrl / st-ctrl  must be no-match with span 32 on EVERY release.
           They are the negative controls; a MATCH in either column
           invalidates the predicate it belongs to.
  repro    is the reporter's shader. Clean on v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010
           only because those builds load the whole struct up front,
           so the per-element path the defect lives in is never used.
  minimal  is the issue body's own snippet and is wrong on every
           release, which is what says the defect is older than the
           v1.6.2104 boundary the reporter's shader shows.
  store    is the write direction: the same doubled stride, so the
           store lands in the NEXT buffer element. Adjacent to the
           issue, which is about loads, and not part of the verdict.
